hook: Look at the pickup pattern printed on a microphone box. It is drawn as a polar graph: in each direction, the distance from the center shows how well the microphone hears. The heart-shaped one is a cardioid, and its equation is a polar function, $r = 1 + \cos\theta$.

prereq.why: The angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$ points into Quadrant I, and $r = -2$ moves backward through the pole into Quadrant III.

figure.caption: The rose $r = 3\sin(2\theta)$: four petals, each reaching distance $3$ from the pole.

chain.effect: the input of $r = f(\theta)$ is the direction

chain.cause: Read $r$ from the graph of $r$ against $\theta$
chain.effect: the output is the signed distance along that direction
the curve passes through the pole
the point is drawn on the opposite ray, in the opposite quadrant

ideas: A polar function $r = f(\theta)$ gives a distance for each direction; the curve is all points $(f(\theta), \theta)$.
Each hump of the graph of $r$ against $\theta$ draws one loop or petal; zeros of $r$ are visits to the pole.
$r = a\cos(n\theta)$ and $r = a\sin(n\theta)$ are roses: $n$ petals if $n$ is odd, $2n$ if $n$ is even.
$r = a + b\cos\theta$ is a limaçon: an inner loop if $|a| < |b|$, a cardioid if $|a| = |b|$, no loop if $|a| > |b|$.

misconception.wrong: Where $r$ is negative, the curve is drawn in the quadrant the angle points to, just closer to the pole.
misconception.right: A negative $r$ sends the point backward through the pole, so it is drawn in the opposite quadrant. That is how the inner loop of $r = 1 + 2\cos\theta$ ends up to the right of the pole.

summary: A polar function $r = f(\theta)$ assigns a signed distance to every direction. Read it from its graph of $r$ against $\theta$: zeros are visits to the pole, negative values are drawn on the opposite ray, and each hump draws a petal or loop. Circles ($r = a$, $r = a\cos\theta$), limaçons and cardioids ($r = a + b\cos\theta$) and roses ($r = a\sin(n\theta)$) are the families to know.
